He had been diagnosed with diabetes 2 years ago, which was controlled by subcutaneously administrating insulin glargine 15 mg daily. He also suffered from hypertension. He had benign prostatic hypertrophy and was treated by post-transurethral resection of the prostate with multiple biopsies, which were all negative for malignancy. He had undergone a colonoscopy 4 years ago, which was normal. He had been smoking a pack of cigarettes per day for 20 years but had stopped doing so from the past 20 years or more. He denied alcohol intake or the use of illicit drugs. His other medications included aspirin 81 mg/d, carvedilol phosphate 10 mg/d, candesartan/hydrochlorothiazide 16 mg/12. 5 mg daily, and felodipine 5 mg daily. When seen in the clinic, he was noted to have a stiff axial posture with rigid back and thigh musculature. He was awake, alert, and oriented to time, place, and person. His memory was intact. The cranial nerves were all intact. He had normal muscle strength, intact sensory perception, 2 /H11001deep tendon reflexes, intact finger-to-nose test, but a stiff gait.

extractions.quote: SPS is characterized by frequently elevated levels of circulating anti-GAD. These antibodies have been shown in vitro to inhibit the activity of GABA, which is the major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system. Reduced levels of GABA in several regions of the brain have been found in patients with typical SPS. This finding gives support to the pathologic role of anti-GAD, and may explain the clinical presentation of SPS. The impaired inhibitory neurotransmission leads to hyperactivity of the peripheral motor unit, resulting in rigidity and spasms.
